boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time around SJSU through its public galleries, arts programming, and a city park.

cards.title: Browse the Thompson Gallery
cards.subtitle: Art & Design Building, Room 127
cards.notes: Plan a weekday visit during the academic semester, then spend time with the current exhibition. Check the gallery page before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery with free public admission during the academic semester.
cards.evidence_claim: The Natalie and James Thompson Gallery states that admission is free and it is open to the public during the academic semester.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information | Natalie and James Thompson Gallery
cards.access_notes: Free public admission is offered during the academic semester; the gallery advises arranging appointments Monday through Friday.

cards.title: Catch a Tuesday art talk
cards.subtitle: Art Building Lecture Hall, Room 133
cards.notes: Arrive for the 5 p.m. public lecture or presentation, then continue into the student-gallery receptions held afterward.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Tuesday evening lecture and gallery-reception program.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU says its Tuesday Open House includes a weekly free public lecture or presentation, with free public registration.
cards.source_title: Events Information | Art and Art History
cards.access_notes: In-person presentations are listed for 5–6 p.m. in Art Building Room 133; confirm the weekly schedule before visiting.

cards.title: See the rotating work in Gallery 5
cards.subtitle: Art Building, Room 107
cards.notes: Visit on a Tuesday reception evening to see the current student exhibition and talk with friends about what is on view.
cards.short_summary: One of SJSU’s named student exhibition galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU identifies Gallery 5 in Art Building Room 107; student-gallery artist receptions on Tuesday evenings are open to the public free of charge.
cards.access_notes: For free Tuesday reception access, use the Art and Art History student-galleries schedule and confirm the current exhibition.

cards.title: Stop into Gallery 3
cards.subtitle: Art Building, Room 112
cards.notes: Make Gallery 3 one stop on a Tuesday evening art walk, allowing time to look closely at the week’s student work.
cards.short_summary: A named Art Building gallery used in SJSU’s student exhibition program.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s Art Building map identifies Gallery 3 in Room 112, and SJSU says Tuesday student-gallery receptions are open to the public free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Free access applies to Tuesday artist receptions; contact the gallery office for other student-gallery hours.

cards.title: Walk through Black Gallery
cards.subtitle: Art Building, Room 204
cards.notes: Head upstairs during the Tuesday reception program and use the gallery as a focused stop for a short, no-cost art break.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor student gallery in SJSU’s Art Building.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s Art Building map identifies Black Gallery in Room 204, and its student-gallery receptions are open to the public free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Free access applies to Tuesday artist receptions; contact the gallery office for other student-gallery hours.

cards.title: Add the Design Gallery to the loop
cards.subtitle: Art Building, Room 212A
cards.notes: Pair this second-floor gallery with Black Gallery on a Tuesday evening, then compare how the exhibitions use different media.
cards.short_summary: A named gallery space in the Art Building’s student exhibition circuit.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s Art Building map identifies the Design Gallery in Room 212A, and SJSU says Tuesday student-gallery receptions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free access applies to Tuesday artist receptions; contact the gallery office for other student-gallery hours.

cards.title: Climb up to Gallery 8
cards.subtitle: Art Building, Room 308
cards.notes: Use the third-floor stop as part of a Tuesday exhibition walk; bring a friend and take time to discuss the work on display.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor student gallery in SJSU’s Art Building.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s Art Building map identifies Gallery 8 in Room 308, while the university says Tuesday student-gallery receptions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free access applies to Tuesday artist receptions; contact the gallery office for other student-gallery hours.

cards.title: Check out Belcher Gallery
cards.subtitle: Art Building, Room 131
cards.notes: Drop in during Tuesday’s reception window and make it a low-key art stop between the lecture and other nearby galleries.
cards.short_summary: A named first-floor gallery in the SJSU Art Building.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s Art Building map identifies Belcher Gallery in Room 131, and the university describes its Tuesday student-gallery receptions as free and public.
cards.access_notes: Free access applies to Tuesday artist receptions; contact the gallery office for other student-gallery hours.

cards.entity_name: Public Art as Resistance in San Jose self-guided tour
cards.title: Follow the public-art self-guided tour
cards.subtitle: Downtown San José, beginning near SJSU
cards.notes: Open the project’s map and take the self-guided route at your own pace to view downtown public art, monuments, and memorials.
cards.short_summary: A map-based downtown public-art activity developed with SJSU participation.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s Public Art as Resistance project describes a self-guided public-art tour using an artistically designed map and Linktree, with activities free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: About this Project | Public Art as Resistance in San Jose
cards.access_notes: Use the project map and follow normal pedestrian-safety practices; no admission or purchase is described for the self-guided activity.

cards.title: Meet at Del Monte Park
cards.subtitle: 806 W Home St, San José
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or a book and use the open grass and picnic areas for an easy daytime meetup without an admission charge.
cards.short_summary: A City of San José park with open space and no admission fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of San José lists Del Monte Park’s admission fee as “No Admission Fee” and identifies open space and picnic areas among its features.
cards.source_title: Del Monte Park | City of San José
cards.access_notes: The City lists park hours as dawn to sunset and notes non-reservable picnic sites.
